questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan aimed at accelerating food grain production, increasing employment and productivity with a focus on 'food, work and productivity'?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Seventh Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seventh Five-Year Plan** (1985-1990) focused on accelerating **food grain production**, increasing **employment**, and improving **productivity**.
 
• This plan aimed to emphasize the themes of '**food, work, and productivity**' to ensure **self-sufficiency** in food production and provide more opportunities for employment.
 
• The **agriculture sector** was given priority, with measures to enhance **irrigation facilities**, improve **seed quality**, and provide better **credit facilities** to farmers.
 
• Special attention was given to the development of **employment-generating programs** like the **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP)** and **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana**.
 
• It also focused on improving **industrial productivity** through the adoption of advanced **technologies** and better management practices.
 
• The plan emphasized **social justice** by targeting benefits for disadvantaged sections, including the **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**, **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**, and **women**.
 
• The Seventh Plan marked a transition towards a greater role for the **private sector** in economic growth, encouraging investment in industries and services.
 
• This plan was successful in achieving a **GDP growth rate** of 5.8% against the targeted 5%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Third Plan**__

 __
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961-1966) focused on building a strong industrial base and achieving **self-reliance** in agriculture and industry.
 
• This plan aimed to increase agricultural production to meet **food requirements** and reduce dependence on imports.
 
• It targeted **community development** and emphasized the expansion of **education**, health, and other social services.
 
• Due to **economic challenges**, including the Indo-China war (1962) and Indo-Pak war (1965), this plan fell short of its objectives.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Plan**__
 __
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan** (1969-1974) focused on achieving **self-reliance** and growth with **stability**.
 
• It aimed at reducing **income inequalities** and improving the standard of living of the **poor**.
 
• The plan emphasized the promotion of **green revolution technologies** to enhance agricultural productivity.
 
• Due to challenges like **inflation**, droughts, and political instability, the plan's goals were not fully realized.
 
 
 
• **Sixth Plan**__
 
 
• The **Sixth Five-Year Plan** (1980-1985) aimed at achieving **poverty alleviation**, economic modernization, and reducing regional disparities.
 
• It introduced programs like **National Rural Employment Program** to increase employment opportunities.
 
• Focus was given to **industrialization**, the development of **infrastructure**, and the promotion of **export-oriented industries**.
 
• The plan was successful in achieving significant economic growth and reducing poverty levels.

questions.question: Who was appointed for a third term as the National Security Advisor in the Modi government in June 2024?

• He was appointed as the **National Security Advisor (NSA) of India** in 2014 during the first term of the Narendra Modi government.
 
• In June 2024, he was reappointed for a **third consecutive term** as the NSA, showcasing the government’s trust in his strategic acumen and leadership abilities.
 
• Ajit Doval is known for his extensive experience in **intelligence, national security, and counter-terrorism operations**.
 
• He played a critical role in the planning and execution of significant operations like the **surgical strikes in 2016** and **Balakot airstrikes in 2019**.
 
• As NSA, he has been instrumental in shaping India’s **national security policies and foreign relations**, particularly in handling sensitive issues with neighbors like Pakistan and China.
 
• Ajit Doval is also the architect of the **Doval Doctrine**, which emphasizes a proactive and assertive approach to counter threats to India’s sovereignty and security.
 
• He is the fifth NSA of India and the first to hold the position for such an extended period, making him a trusted advisor to the government on critical matters.
 
• His tenure is marked by a focus on **modernizing India’s defense and intelligence infrastructure** and fostering international cooperation on security matters.

• **Shivshankar Menon**__

 __
 
• **Shivshankar Menon** is a distinguished Indian diplomat who served as the **National Security Advisor** from 2010 to 2014 during the tenure of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.
 
• He is known for his expertise in **foreign policy and international relations**, particularly his role in shaping India’s Look East Policy.
 
• Menon also played a pivotal role in the **India-US Civil Nuclear Agreement** and was India’s ambassador to key countries like China and Pakistan.

questions.question: Which birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi was celebrated on 2ⁿd October 2023?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is 154th .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 154th **birth anniversary** of **Mahatma Gandhi** was celebrated on **2nd October 2023**.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi**, is one of the most celebrated leaders in **Indian history** and is regarded as the **Father of the Nation** in India.
 
• He was born on **2nd October 1869** in **Porbandar, Gujarat.**
 
• Gandhi is globally known for his philosophy of **non-violence (Ahimsa)** and his role in India's **freedom struggle** against British rule.
 
• This day is commemorated worldwide as the **International Day of Non-Violence**, as declared by the **United Nations General Assembly** in 2007.
 
• On this occasion, tributes are paid to Mahatma Gandhi at his **samadhi at Raj Ghat** in New Delhi, where prayers, cultural events, and exhibitions are organized.
 
• The day is marked by activities such as **cleanliness drives** under the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, which was inspired by Gandhi's vision of a clean and self-reliant India.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's principles of **Satyagraha (truth force)** and civil disobedience have influenced many leaders and movements worldwide, including Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi's Contributions:**__

 __
 
• He led various movements such as the **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)**, the **Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)**, and the **Quit India Movement (1942)**.
 
• He pioneered the philosophy of **self-reliance (Swadeshi)**, encouraging Indians to boycott British goods and promote local industries.
 
• He emphasized the importance of **communal harmony** and worked tirelessly to bridge gaps between various communities in India.
 
• His autobiography, **"The Story of My Experiments with Truth,"** is widely read and provides deep insights into his personal journey and philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 2nd October:**__
 
 
• The day is observed as a national holiday in India to honor Mahatma Gandhi's contributions to the nation.
 
• It is also celebrated as **Lal Bahadur Shastri Jayanti**, as **Lal Bahadur Shastri**, India's second Prime Minister, was born on the same day in **1904**.
 
• Globally, the day is recognized as a symbol of peace and non-violence.

questions.question: A standard rain gauge is a meteorological instrument consisting of a collector of what shape connected to a measuring tube that is used to measure rainfall per unit area at a given time?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Funnel-shaped**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A standard **rain gauge** is a meteorological instrument used to measure the amount of **rainfall** over a specific area during a given period.
 
• The gauge consists of a **funnel-shaped collector** designed to direct rainwater into a measuring tube.
 
• The funnel shape is essential for efficiently channeling rainwater into the tube, ensuring accurate measurement.
 
• The measuring tube is calibrated to precisely measure rainfall, typically in units like **millimeters** or **inches**.
 
• Rain gauges are widely used in **meteorological studies**, agriculture, hydrology, and environmental monitoring.
 
• The funnel design prevents water from spilling and minimizes evaporation, leading to reliable data collection.
 
• Standard rain gauges are typically placed in open areas, free from obstructions like trees or buildings, to ensure accurate rainfall measurement.
 
• The data collected from rain gauges are used to study weather patterns, manage water resources, and predict **floods** or **droughts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** J-shaped**__

 __
 
• A **J-shaped design** is not used in standard rain gauges as it is not effective for collecting and channeling rainwater.
 
• This shape is more commonly associated with pipe or tube designs for other applications, such as plumbing or fluid dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Disc-shaped**__
 __
 
• A **disc-shaped design** does not effectively collect and channel rainwater for measurement.
 
• This shape might be suitable for **other meteorological instruments** like barometers or thermometers but is not practical for rain gauges.
 
 
 
• **Prism-shaped**__
 
 
• The **prism-shaped design** is rarely used in rain gauges as it lacks the ability to efficiently channel water into a measuring tube.
 
• Prism shapes are more commonly used in optical instruments like **prisms** for light refraction or dispersion.

questions.question: What is the average monthly income per agricultural household in India, according to the 77th round of National Statistical Office (NSO) survey, calculated using the paid-out expenses approach?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**₹ 10,218**__.

__
 
• The **77th Round of the National Statistical Office (NSO) Survey** provides critical data on the socio-economic conditions of **agricultural households in India**.
 
• According to this survey, the **average monthly income** per agricultural household in India, calculated using the **paid-out expenses approach**, is **₹ 10,218**.
 
• This figure includes income from various sources such as:
 
 
• **Wages and salaries**
 
• **Crop production**
 
• **Livestock** and allied activities
 
• **Non-farm business activities**
 
• Other forms of income like **leasing out land** or **remittances**.
 
 
 
• The survey highlights that **agricultural households** in India face **incomes disparities**, with significant variations across states, regions, and landholding sizes.
 
• The data is instrumental for policymakers to design **welfare programs** and schemes aimed at improving the **livelihoods** of farmers.
 
• It also provides insights into the **economic viability** of farming as a profession in modern India.
 
• The approach used in this survey is the **paid-out expenses approach**, which accounts for the cost incurred by farmers on inputs like **fertilizers, seeds, labor, and other resources**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• The **NSO survey** is a key tool used by the government to assess the **economic conditions of households**, particularly those engaged in **agriculture**.
 
• Data from the survey is used to gauge **farmers’ income levels**, helping to inform and assess the effectiveness of schemes like **PM-KISAN**, **Kisan Credit Card**, and **crop insurance programs**.
 
• The survey also identifies **areas of improvement** in agricultural policy, such as access to credit, market linkages, and input subsidies.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Highlighted**__
 __
 
• The data underscores the **low earnings** from agriculture, with many farmers relying on **non-agricultural sources** for additional income.
 
• It points to the **need for diversification** of income sources and improved **pricing mechanisms** for agricultural produce.
 
• The survey also reflects issues such as **lack of access to modern technology, irrigation facilities**, and **market infrastructure**.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a person to be considered literate in the Indian Census?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**7 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Indian Census**, the term "literacy" is defined as the ability of a person to read and write in any language.
 
• The **minimum age** considered for literacy in the Indian Census is **7 years**.
 
• A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language is considered **literate**.
 
• This definition excludes individuals below the age of 7, as it is assumed that children younger than 7 years are still in the process of acquiring basic literacy skills.
 
• The literacy rate is a significant indicator of the **educational development** and **socio-economic status** of a country.
 
• The Indian Census collects data on literacy to study trends in education and to formulate policies for improving access to education.
 
• The **Census of India** is conducted every 10 years and includes detailed surveys on literacy, population, and other demographic factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **10 years**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect as the **Indian Census** considers individuals aged **7 years and above** for literacy calculations, not 10 years.
 
• While some organizations or studies may use different age thresholds for literacy, the Census of India specifically uses the **7-year mark**.
 
 
 
• **5 years**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because children aged 5 years are typically at the stage of early education and are not considered in literacy calculations by the **Census of India**.
 
• At this age, most children are learning basic reading and writing skills, which are not sufficient for qualifying as literate.
 
 
 
• **15 years**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect as it represents a much higher threshold than what is set by the **Indian Census**.
 
• The Census uses the age of **7 years** to include a broader population in literacy calculations.
 
• If the threshold were set at 15 years, it would exclude a large number of literate children and adolescents below that age.

questions.question: Which language and script were primarily used in Ashoka's edicts?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Prakrit and Brahmi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka's edicts** were primarily written in the **Prakrit language**, which was the common language spoken by the masses during his time.
 
• The script used in most of the edicts was **Brahmi**, which is one of the earliest scripts used in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The use of **Prakrit and Brahmi** reflects Ashoka's effort to communicate his messages of **Dhamma** (moral law and nonviolence) to the majority of the population in a language they could understand.
 
• The inscriptions were carved on **pillars, rocks, and caves**, strategically located across the empire to ensure maximum reach.
 
• Some of the edicts were also written in **Kharoshti** script and other regional languages, depending on the geographical location.
 
• The messages in the edicts emphasized **ethical conduct**, **religious tolerance**, and the welfare of all beings, showcasing Ashoka's commitment to peace and governance.
 
• The Brahmi script later evolved into several scripts, including **Devanagari**, which is used in modern languages like Hindi and Sanskrit.
 
• The use of **Prakrit and Brahmi** in Ashoka's edicts marked a significant step in making royal decrees accessible to the common people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Sanskrit and Devanagari**__

 __
 
• **Sanskrit** was a language primarily used for religious and scholarly purposes during ancient times and later became central to Hindu scriptures and texts.
 
• The **Devanagari script** emerged much later and is widely used for modern Indian languages like Hindi, Marathi, and Sanskrit.
 
• Sanskrit and Devanagari were not used in Ashoka's edicts as they were not intended for scholarly or religious elites but for the common people.
 
 
 
• ** Pali and Kharoshti**__
 __
 
• **Pali** was used in Buddhist texts, including the **Tripitaka**, and was closely related to Prakrit.
 
• **Kharoshti script** was used in certain regions of Ashoka's empire, particularly in the northwest areas like present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• Although some of Ashoka's edicts were written in Kharoshti, it was not the primary script or language used across the empire.
 
 
 
• ** Greek and Latin**__
 
 
• **Greek** was used in Ashoka's edicts located in the far-western regions of his empire, like Kandahar, as a result of cultural interaction with the Hellenistic world.
 
• **Latin** was never used in Ashoka's edicts; it was a language of the Roman Empire, which had no direct connection to Mauryan India.

questions.question: Which alkyne with chemical formula CH₃C≡CH appears as a colourless liquefied gas with a sweet odour?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1-Propyne**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1-Propyne**, also known as methylacetylene, is a chemical compound with the formula **CH₃C≡CH**.
 
• It is an **alkyne**, which is a hydrocarbon containing a carbon-carbon triple bond, making it unsaturated.
 
• **1-Propyne** is a **colorless liquefied gas** under standard conditions and has a **sweet odor**.
 
• Due to its triple bond, it exhibits **reactivity** in various chemical reactions, such as polymerization and addition reactions.
 
• This compound is part of the **propyne family** and is a common building block in organic synthesis and industrial chemical processes.
 
• It is also used in specialized applications, such as in welding and cutting, where it is blended with **propylene** and other hydrocarbons.
 
• The presence of the **terminal triple bond** makes 1-propyne distinct from other hydrocarbons, including its isomer propadiene.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ethyne**__

 __
 
• **Ethyne**, commonly known as acetylene, has the chemical formula **C₂H₂**.
 
• It is the simplest alkyne and is widely used as a fuel in welding and cutting processes due to its high flame temperature.
 
• Unlike 1-propyne, ethyne is not a liquefied gas under standard conditions; it exists as a gas at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **1-Hexyne**__
 __
 
• **1-Hexyne** is a higher alkyne with the formula **C₆H₁₀**, containing six carbon atoms.
 
• It is a liquid at room temperature and does not share the sweet odor or gaseous nature of 1-propyne.
 
• It is used in organic synthesis but is not related to applications like 1-propyne.
 
 
 
• **1-Butyne**__
 
 
• **1-Butyne**, with the formula **C₄H₆**, is a smaller alkyne compared to 1-Hexyne but larger than 1-Propyne.
 
• It is a gas at standard conditions but lacks the distinct sweet odor associated with 1-Propyne.
 
• It is used in organic synthesis but is not as commonly encountered as ethyne or 1-propyne.
